mechanism.summary: Extend the direct-leaf construct path to base class constructors and stop paying a call per literal field initializer. A base class construction ran through the general function_env (two received-upvalue scans, name-keyed home-object and super-constructor inserts with their String allocations, a cloned instance-element vector) and then called one direct-leaf thunk per instance field, so `new Vector(x, y, z)` with three `= 0` fields cost four activations. Now (1) a field initializer whose whole body is `return <literal>` is read as its constant (Bytecode::constant_return, classified at build time); (2) a constructor's instance-element list is shared behind an Rc instead of cloned per construction; (3) a base class constructor whose body the slot-seeding predicate admits and whose instance elements are all public string-keyed fields with literal or direct-leaf initializers builds its receiver, installs its fields with the existing shared-key write (falling back to the general define, and its TypeError, when an earlier initializer made the receiver reject the key), and runs on the direct-leaf frame with new.target seeded.
mechanism.generality: Admission is decided from the constructor's own shape (base class, slot-seedable body, public string-keyed fields, literal or direct-leaf initializers) and memoized on the function; it never inspects benchmark names, source paths, property spellings, values, iteration counts, or results. Derived classes, private elements, symbol-keyed fields, and non-leaf initializers keep the general path unchanged. Literal field initializers are the dominant class-field shape in idiomatic code (`x = 0`, `p = null`, `flag = false`); the constant read applies on both the direct and the general construct path.
semantic_risks: a literal initializer read must be indistinguishable from calling the thunk: the body `return <literal>` has no side effects and cannot observe this or new.target

field installation order, the enumerable/writable/configurable data-property shape, and the TypeError for a receiver that an earlier initializer made non-extensible or that already holds the key must match initialize_instance_fields
an initializer thunk runs with this = the receiver and new.target undefined, exactly as before
the constructor body still sees new.target = the constructor and a strict this, and a primitive completion yields the receiver
sharing the instance-element list must copy-on-write when class definition appends elements while an earlier snapshot is alive

profile_evidence.shared_cost: Of 2,641 in-process samples, the general construct path takes 117 in function_env, 50 in construct_function, 32 in eval_function_bytecode, 26 in run_prepared_bytecode_call, 25 in apply_call_env, 27 in initialize_instance_fields, 26 in SipHash and 23 in FrameBindings::get for the name-keyed bindings, and about 270 (10%) in malloc/free for the per-construction strings and element vector; the per-field direct-leaf thunk calls add to the 112 new_with_globals and 51 eval_direct_call_bytecode samples. Every class in the case (Vector, Color, Ray, IntersectionInfo, Light, Camera, Scene, Material, Shape) is a base class with literal-initialized public fields or a derived class of one.
